headlineHtml: H1 FY27: operating profit up 161% on AI data-centre demand; guidance raised and dividend doubled — focus shifts to the implied H2 step-down
ledeHtml: Table 1 Fujikura's H1 FY27 operating profit rose 161% YoY to ¥235.0bn on AI data-centre demand for optical fibre and cabling, and the company raised full-year guidance and doubled the dividend. The debate now moves to the second half: guidance implies H2 operating profit of ¥194bn, below the H1 print.

bullets.html: H1 FY27 (Apr–Sep 2026) sales were ¥867.4bn (+55.2% YoY), operating profit ¥235.0bn (+160.6%) and net profit ¥180.3bn (+168.5%). Information & Communications segment OP of ¥217.7bn (+195.0%) did the heavy lifting — AI data-centre cabling is the P&L.
FY27 guidance now stands at sales of ¥1,768bn, operating profit of ¥429bn and net profit of ¥326bn. The annual dividend was raised from ¥38 to ¥80 per share.
Against the raised guide, H1 delivered 49.1% of full-year sales, 54.8% of operating profit and 55.3% of net profit — an unusually front-loaded year even for a strong AI-capex cycle.

bullets.leadHtml: The implied H2 is the debate.
bullets.html: Guidance minus H1 implies H2 operating profit of ¥194bn, a step down from ¥235bn in H1. Whether that is conservatism or a genuine order slowdown is the question the Q3 print has to answer. The shares closed at ¥2,906 on 13 Nov, roughly 63% below the May 2026 high on a six-month view.

blocks.heading: H1 FY2027 results — the numbers
blocks.html:
Fujikura reported H1 FY27 results on 10 November. Sales of ¥867.4bn rose 55.2% YoY; operating profit of ¥235.0bn rose 160.6%; net profit of ¥180.3bn rose 168.5%. The Information & Communications segment — optical fibre, fusion splicers and data-centre cabling — generated ¥217.7bn of operating profit, up 195.0% YoY, and accounts for almost all of the group's profit pool.

Standalone Q2 (Jul–Sep) sales were about ¥465bn, up from about ¥402bn in Q1, so momentum was still building into the autumn rather than fading after a single strong quarter. Table 1 Figure 1

blocks.heading: Guidance and the implied second half
blocks.html:
The raised FY27 guide — sales ¥1,768bn, OP ¥429bn, net ¥326bn — embeds a second half that is weaker than the first: implied H2 sales of about ¥901bn and implied H2 OP of ¥194bn, against ¥235bn achieved in H1. Japanese corporates habitually guide conservatively at the H1 stage, and the dividend doubling to ¥80 signals management confidence in cash generation.

What would settle the question is order commentary: hyperscaler capex plans for calendar 2027, fibre and cable allocation, and any capacity additions. A Q3 print that keeps the quarterly OP run-rate near the H1 average would make the implied H2 look like sandbagging; a sequential drop would validate it.

blocks.heading: What we watch next
blocks.html:
Three items. First, the Q3 FY27 print (expected February 2027): quarterly OP against the roughly ¥117bn H1 quarterly average, and any revision to the FY guide. Second, US hyperscaler capex commentary through the December quarter — Fujikura's Information & Communications segment is a direct read-across. Third, the share price itself: at ¥2,906 the stock trades on 26.3x trailing earnings (Finnhub, 13 Nov) after a six-month fall of about 63%, so expectations have already reset hard.
